title: knapsack-surge-efficiency-latency-cost-notes
summary: Working notes for a compact collateral piece comparing model variants and runtime configs on short microbursts and sustained surges. Introduces a compact metric (surge_efficiency) to trade off latency penalties vs throughput gains under constrained GPU slots.
test_setup: Single-region test cluster: 8xA100 (40GB) pooled, main serving runtime at commit a9f3c6, scheduler=tiling+slot-pacing experimental branch. Traffic generator: synthetic conversation mixer (60% short-turn, 30% medium, 10% long) with Poisson arrival and configurable spike windows. Measurements aggregated over 30m runs with 10x microburst injections (100–2,500 concurrent requests over 10s). Cost model: instance-hour prorated + GPU-hour, normalized to $ per 1k tokens produced at average 32 token reply. All runs repeated 5 times; median reported.
workload_profile: Microburst-focused: 10s spike, baseline 50 RPS, spike peak up to 2500 concurrent. Session lengths: short=6 tokens, medium=48 tokens, long=240 tokens. Focus on p50/p90/p99 latency and token-unit cost during spike window vs baseline.
raw_results: scenario | model | quant | p50(ms) | p90(ms) | p99(ms) | tokens/k | $/k tokens

derived_metrics: Definition: surge_efficiency = throughput_gain_over_baseline / latency_penalty_at_p99 (normalized). Higher is better.
Throughput gain measured as tokens/k during spike divided by baseline tokens/k.
Examples computed from runs: hybrid: throughput_gain=0.68/1.00=0.68, latency_penalty=410/480=0.854 => surge_efficiency=0.68/0.854=0.80
key_takeaways: Quantized smaller models (m3-7b int4) give best cost efficiency and most favorable surge_efficiency — lower absolute throughput but much smaller latency penalties under microbursts.
Tiling/slotized approaches reduce cost per token vs fp16 baseline but at the expense of p99 tail, making them less attractive for latency-sensitive SLAs during spikes.
Multiplexing can increase sustained tokens/k but amplifies tail latency dramatically during short spikes — useful for batch-y workloads but risky for interactive apps.
Prefetch heuristics offer a middle ground: modest cost wins with manageable tails if prefetch budgets are tuned conservatively.
Surge_efficiency is a compact way to summarize the trade-off but must be reported alongside absolute p99 to avoid masking unacceptable tails.
recommendations: For customer-facing collateral: produce a two-panel graphic showing (1) cost per 1k tokens vs p99 during spike and (2) surge_efficiency vs absolute p99. Messaging: 'Pick the model+quant combo that meets your SLA—compressed models win for heavy microburst environments; slotization best for steady throughput but test tails.' Internally: run N=20 repeats for top 3 configs to tighten p99 CI; iterate prefetch window from 50–250ms to find knee. Consider a small 'knapsack' decision aid in Console that ranks configs by user constraints (max-p99, budget per 1k tokens).
open_questions: How does client-side retry/backoff interact with observed p99 inflation in slotized mode? Need an end-to-end sim with retries.
Are our cost numbers aligned to commercial pricing (marketplace) when GPU/hour amortization includes idle scheduling overhead? Ask finance to validate.
